fieldMappings.reason: Simple product price on its single default variant: a sale price below the regular price becomes actualPrice and the regular price the compare-at price; otherwise the regular price is actualPrice. A WPC bundle (woosb) is written at its own selling price `price`, never regular_price (the sum of its parts); when `price` is 0 or below it falls back to its sale price, then its regular price (each only above 0), else the product is written hidden at 0 with the product-price-missing task. A sale price of 0 or below is never a sale. A bundle has no compare-at price unless the choice woosb-compare-at says so.

fieldMappings.reason: Each WooCommerce variation becomes a Wix variant; its attribute values become option choices, resolved from term slugs to the parent's display names. An attribute that is "Any" in every variation cannot change price or stock, so it becomes a mandatory modifier on one default variant (owner-approved rule); the product step writes its customization just before the product. A tracked stock pool is never copied onto several variants. A variation value the parent does not declare is held (selection-route-contradiction), never guessed.

product-variations-missing.action: Requires Import Operator: these variable products came without their variations, so they were held.

product-variations-missing.importOperatorPrompt: Re-read /wc/v3/products/{id}/variations for the listed products into data/source-extract/product-variation.ndjson and rerun the product import for these source ids.

selection-route-contradiction.action: Each of these products has a variation set to a value the product no longer offers (for example an old size), so it was not imported. Fix or delete that variation in WooCommerce and ask for a rerun, or add the product in Business Manager.
selection-route-contradiction.resolutionEvidence: Each listed product exists in Wix with its options.

product-brand-reference-missing.action: Requires Import Operator: these products were not imported because their brand could not be linked (it is missing from the WooCommerce brands, or its import failed). A product is never imported without its brand unless the owner asks for that.
product-brand-reference-missing.resolutionEvidence: Each listed product is imported with its brand, or the owner's choice to import it without a brand is recorded.
product-brand-reference-missing.importOperatorPrompt: For each listed product, check its brand in WooCommerce (Products > Brands). If the brand is missing, restore it, re-extract and rerun the product-brand import (stores/brand), then rerun the product import for these source ids with --deferred-only. If the brand import failed, fix that failure and rerun both imports. If the owner wants these products now without a brand, record that as an approved omission and resume the product import with --deferred-only.

product-description-too-long.action: These products have a description over 16,000 characters and were not imported. Shorten the description in the source and ask for a rerun, or add the product in Business Manager.
product-description-too-long.resolutionEvidence: Each listed product exists in Wix.

product-weight-invalid.action: These products have a weight that is not a number in the source and were not imported. Fix the weight in WooCommerce and ask for a rerun, or add the product in Business Manager.

product-options-over-limit.action: These products have more variation attributes than Wix Stores allows (6 options), so they were not imported. For each, add the product in Business Manager with the options and prices you want shoppers to see (for example fewer options, or separate products).

builderContract: Each fieldMappings row names one export of product.builder.js (helper "<file>#<export>"). lib/plan-builder.js calls it with (record, {lookups, choices, args}) and merges its canonical part into one wix-build buildProduct call; tags and categories are toolkit reference helpers. A row whose helper names its own hold codes keeps valuePolicy.invalid without a code, so the helper code reaches the journal.
